title: Evaluating AI Counseling in Japanese: Counselor, Client, and Evaluator Roles Assessed by Motivational Interviewing Criteria

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the scoring leniency and metric-specific preferences of AI evaluators (o3, Sonnet, Gemini) against human expert ratings using the Motivational Interviewing Treatment Integrity (MITI) coding manual.

Using linear mixed-effects models to test whether the specified age demographic of the simulated client (20s, 40s, or 60s) significantly alters the counseling evaluation scores assigned by AI and human evaluators.
Using linear mixed-effects models to test whether the specified sex of the simulated client (male or female) significantly alters the counseling evaluation scores assigned by AI and human evaluators.

Qualitative assessment by human experts to identify unnatural dialogue patterns in client AIs, specifically noting an LLM characteristic of 'positive compliance bias' where models unconditionally accept suggestions and display minimal resistance.
